#2007. How 'football geek' Kim Hellberg turned Middlesbrough into the 'PSG of the Championship' - thanks to 'Del Boy and Rodney', the next Harry Kane and the transfer strategy that's taken them to a new level

Published: 13:14 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 08:53 EDT, 30 October 2026

I was sat in the press conference room at St Mary’s Stadium back in May when Kim Hellberg forced back tears as he talked about everything he’d sacrificed. All the time spent away from his family, all those nights when he called them to say he wouldn’t be coming home because he had more Southampton matches to watch.

And despite them all, there the Middlesbrough manager still sat, beaten in the second leg of the Championship play-off semi-final by a manager who sent staff to spy on his training session and who was, for now, going to Wembley.

‘I have nothing to say to him,’ Hellberg had replied when asked if he had spoken to Southampton boss Tonda Eckert. Hellberg had already completed his TV and local radio interviews but informed club staff that he still had things, about sacrifices, that he wanted to say.

In the end, of course, it was not over for Hellberg and Boro. Thanks to Daily Mail Sport’s stunning Spygate exclusive, Saints were eventually expelled and Boro went to Wembley in their place. By then, though, the chaos had taken its toll. Those who saw Hellberg in the build-up to the play-off final described him as exhausted and drained.

As did his players, who were left in limbo as they tried, somehow, to remain fit and alert. Luke Ayling, the club’s captain, found out they were going to Wembley while he was bathing his young son just days before the final. Middlesbrough lost to Hull, and had to prepare for a 10th successive season in the Championship. They should have gone up automatically but blew it, having spent most of the season second in the table.

All of that madness and heartbreak could, quite easily, have left Boro with too many scars and yet they host Charlton this weekend sitting top of the Championship, on a 10-game unbeaten run. Somehow, Boro have kicked on again and sources close to the dressing room believe they are better set than ever for a return to the top flight.

Kim Hellberg has led Middlesbrough to the top of the Championship as they banish all memories of Spygate

Aidan Morris celebrates scoring against Burnley last month - Boro are flying as they welcome Charlton on Saturday on a 10-game unbeaten run

For a start, Spygate has barely been mentioned. There’s been no talk of it, according to club insiders, except to discuss the impending return to St Mary’s at the end of November, one which everyone expects to be poisonous.

That has certainly not been helped by the FA’s decision to, effectively, let Eckert off scot free, and how much the Saints and their fans have appeared to revel in it. ‘Everyone in football knows it’s nonsense,’ said one source.

Boro, meanwhile, have just got better. It helps when you play like Paris Saint-Germain. ‘People might laugh,’ said Hellberg, who twice made a point last week of claiming Boro’s style of play shows similarities to the French giants. Hellberg watched PSG’s clash with Barcelona in the Champions League and was drawn to the similar ‘massive spaces’ left in their midfield as they look to be brave in attack.

That is how Hellberg wants his side to play, as risky as it sometimes looks to the casual observer, because it means creating a horde of good chances. They have the most xG (expected goals, which measures the quality of chances created) of any team in the league. Their 'expected goal difference', the gulf between the chances they create and concede, has rocketed since Hellberg took over from Rob Edwards almost a year ago.

Now, they have the player they needed to take those chances in striker Will Lankshear, the Championship’s top scorer, who has recently been labelled the ‘next Harry Kane’. No pressure.

Having been released by Arsenal, then gone through the Tottenham academy (via Sheffield United) before being sent out on loan to several clubs, there are plenty of parallels there, not least because Lankshear is proving himself to be one of the most lethal English strikers around.

His 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland. Like Kane, he’s a superb technical finisher.

There was some surprise when Tottenham agreed to sell him in the summer for an initial £8million that could rise to £20m. But with Roberto De Zerbi showing little interest in academy players, Lankshear knew he had to make a move to get game time. Spurs inserted a matching rights clause should anyone try to swoop in for him.

Will Lankshear's 11 goals so far in the Championship make him the leading scorer across the top four divisions of English football, with two more than Erling Haaland

Sources close to the dressing room talk of a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers from elsewhere in the Championship, Europe, and Premier League, including Leeds, because he knew he would be given the minutes to flourish, in a team that creates heaps of chances and just needed someone to finish them off.

‘I’ve learnt as much as I have my whole life in one week under Kim,’ said Lankshear recently.

So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders. Hellberg rested him for their recent game against Cardiff, only for the 21-year-old to come off the bench to score the equaliser. You suspect he won’t be making the same mistake again.

Sources describe Hellberg as a ‘football geek’. He grew up, like many men in their 30s, playing Football Manager. When previewing Boro’s trip to Bolton last week, a thumping 5-1 win that sent them top, Hellberg said he hadn’t been there before but remembered playing against the likes of Jay-Jay Okocha and Kevin Nolan on the video game. One of his heroes, Frank Lampard, phoned him to offer some words of advice ahead of the play-off final.

Hellberg celebrated the Bolton win by rewatching the game three times. He’d likely have watched it more if they lost.

When he was asked by a Charlton reporter last season if he had ever been to the Valley, Hellberg revealed he had with his dad Stefan, also a football coach in Sweden, during tours of a few grounds in London when he was a young boy.

Hellberg is described as a hands-on coach, one who likes to bombard his players with video clips about the minutiae of their game, and their opponents'. He’s hot on his data. Those who see him week in, week out, say he’s forever dropping stats into conversations and press conferences.

His first role was in the part-time Swedish seventh tier, during which he worked as a gymnastics teacher, and in a kindergarten teaching three to six-year-olds. ‘They are more like the players than you think,’ said Hellberg.

Sources talk of Lankshear as a thoughtful, intelligent lad – ‘his head’s screwed on right,’ says one – who left money on the table to join Boro despite more lucrative offers

So much of Boro’s hopes, say insiders, rest on Lankshear’s shoulders

As with many clubs on the rise – and on the slide – the foundations for that success, or failure, come from far above the grass. Just days after the Wembley heartache, Hellberg sat down with head of football Kieran Scott and head of recruitment Chris Jones to draw up their plans and key targets for the summer. Boro landed most of them.

They beat lots of clubs to Lankshear, whom they had tracked for a while. They snapped up Ashley Phillips, also from Spurs, who was their top defensive target. And Radek Vitek, from Manchester United, their top goalkeeper target.

The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’. Adilson Malanda, the French centre back, was described by one source as the ‘nearest we’ve had to Jonathan Woodgate since Jonathan Woodgate’.

‘We signed the quality that we didn’t have 12 months ago,’ said one club insider. ‘They are a level better. That’s the huge difference.’ This is what Boro have got really good at. Signing players to improve them, develop them, and sell them on at a huge profit.

Scott and Jones, who describe themselves as ‘Del Boy and Rodney’ due to their constant need to sell the club to potential signings who might have glitzier offers, don’t have hordes of analysts but sit there themselves with data software SkillCorner and StatsBomb. And it’s working.

A report by the CIES Football Observatory showed that Boro’s players have appreciated in value by nearly £150m over the last five years – the ninth-highest total in the country, ahead of Villa and Arsenal and just behind Chelsea.

They consistently make a profit on their stars. They signed Morgan Rogers for £1m in 2023 only to sell him to Villa for up to £17m seven months later. When he joined Chelsea this summer for £117m, they banked another £21m as a world-record sell-on fee.

Finn Azaz signed for £2m and was sold to Saints for £12m. Emmanuel Latte Lath, signed for £5m and flogged for £22.5m. Rav van den Berg, signed for less than £500k and sold for £11m.

The loan arrival of Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry was described as the ‘icing on the cake’

Morgan Rogers (centre) was bought for £2m, sold for £17m seven months later and earned Boro another £21m in sell-on fees when he moved to Chelsea this summer

‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together’

Academy players have brought in huge profits, too. Like Hayden Hackney, who joined Everton in the summer for £16.5m, Djed Spence, who headed for Spurs in a move worth up to £20m and Marcus Tavernier, who signed for Bournemouth for £12m. As Del Boy would say, lovely jubbly.

The last time Boro lost in the play-off final, to Norwich in 2015, chairman and owner Steve Gibson gave a rousing speech to his troops to promise they would come back stronger, and they did. They went up automatically the following season. There is a similar feeling now around Teesside.

Club insiders talk of the strongest bond between the club and the community since the days of Juninho and Fabrizio Ravanelli in the 90s. Their attendances, in what is the year of their 150th anniversary, are their highest since they were last in the Premier League.

‘There is something special happening around this place,’ said one source. ‘On the field, off the field, recruitment. Everything is coming together.’

#2005. Frank McAvennie apologises after criticising Celtic star's grief absence

Former Celtic striker Frank McAvennie has apologised after criticising Auston Trusty for missing games after the death of his father.

The defender went public two weeks ago after sadly losing his dad, paying tribute to him online on October 21.

He sat out games against Celta Vigo, Hibs, Dundee United and Falkirk. In the build-up to the latter, manager Martin O'Neill revealed Trusty was heading back to America to "celebrate his dad's life."

McAvennie was critical of how much football the defender was missing, saying on the Let Me Be Frank podcast: "I've got every respect for that, but how long do you want off? Martin (O'Neill) says he's away to celebrate the life of his dad.

"Celebrate the life? You've got football. You're getting paid and we're in trouble. How long is it going to be?

Former Rangers player to stand trial accused of killing woman in road collision £750,000 padel club with four covered courts to open at Ayr United’s stadium

"It's nonsense. My dad was the best man, the only man I looked up to when he died, but you've got to get on with it."

The comments prompted outrage online, with the pundit accused of being insensitive.

That has prompted an apology in the form of an online statement.

McAvennie said: "I’ve seen some of the reaction to comments I made on the podcast about Auston’s absence from football following the death of his father.

"I can understand why people feel my comments were insensitive, and looking back, I should have chosen my words more carefully.

"Everyone deals with grief differently, and I certainly meant no disrespect to Auston or his family. Celtic need the big man back, and that’s what I was clumsily trying to say.

"I wish him and his family all the very best."

#2004. Scotland Women learn Nations League draw after promotion back to League A

Scotland Women will face Germany in the Nations League after the draw was conducted on Tuesday.

Melissa Andreatta’s side were drawn in Group A4 along with the Germans, the Netherlands and Sweden.

Scotland won promotion back to League A after remaining unbeaten in the Women’s World Cup group stage qualifiers earlier this year.

The Nations League fixtures will begin in February 2027.

Scotland are already set to take on the Swedes in round two of World Cup qualifying in December.

Frank McAvennie apologises after criticising Celtic star's grief absence Former Rangers player to stand trial accused of killing woman in road collision

They also previously faced Germany and the Netherlands in the 2025 Nations League.

Meanwhile, also in League A, European champions England were drawn against France, Austria and Portugal in Group A2.

Wales were pulled out in Group A3 alongside Denmark, Italy and Iceland.

In Group B3, Northern Ireland were drawn out with Poland, Finland and Belarus.

Meanwhile, the Republic of Ireland landed a tough task with Nations League holders Spain in their group along with Norway and Switzerland.

The Nations League will play a key role in determining qualification for both the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles and the 2029 Women's European Championship in Germany.

The winners of League A's four groups will advance to the Nations League Finals in October and automatically secure a place at the expanded Olympic Games. Meanwhile, the team finishing bottom of each League A group will drop down to League B.

Teams ending the campaign third in League A will enter promotion/relegation play-offs against runners-up from League B.

For Northern Ireland, who are competing in League B, topping their group would ensure promotion to League A, while a second-place finish would earn a place in the promotion play-offs.

At the other end of the table, the last-placed team in each League B group will be relegated automatically, along with the two worst-performing third-placed sides.

#2003. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

"Incredible talent." 🌟Steven Gerrard reacts to Liverpool's pursuit of Bradley Barcola.🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/bVd7odopa3

"It was the shared vision." 🤝Oliver Glasner on why he chose to join the Nottingham Forest project 👀 pic.twitter.com/ldxjwU8FW4

"For me, it's a special game, definitely." ❤️Andoni Iraola looks ahead to his first Premier League game at Anfield as Liverpool boss.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fukilMigKz

Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Munoz, Wirtz, Gakpo, Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Araujo, Gravenberch, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Aina, Schlager, McAtee, Williams, Ndoye, Gibbs-White, Igor Jesus.

Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Hudson-Odoi, Dominguez, Wood, Delap, Yates, Netz, Abbott.

It's good to be back 😍 @Expedia pic.twitter.com/IGv6d9Pbhq

Having only joined up with his teammates a couple of days ago, new signing Liam Delap begins his Nottingham Forest career on the bench, with Igor Jesus preferred as the central striker.

Lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J

Andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2002. England Under 15s in new World Cup chaos as their opponents REFUSE to face last-minute penalty, giving them an empty net, before the Young Lions have to step in to defend the referee

Published: 06:19 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 09:07 EDT, 30 October 2026

England's Under-15 World Cup campaign has once again been thrown into turmoil after they beat Bolivia with an uncontested last-kick penalty.

The Young Lions were awarded a controversial 41st-minute penalty after West Ham's Emmanuel Famokun was brought down, despite the contact appearing to take place outside the box.

It sparked furious protests from the Bolivian players, who immediately surrounded the referee.

In extraordinary scenes, a coach marched onto the pitch and pointed to the spot where the challenge had taken place.

The referee subsequently issued multiple cards to members of the Bolivian backroom staff. When another coach also entered the pitch, someone on the England bench shouted: 'Send him off as well.'

In protest, the Bolivian players moved away from the penalty area and gathered by the touchline while the kick was taken.

Bolivia refused to defend against an England penalty in fresh U15 World Cup controversy (Source: DAZN)

Their goalkeeper stood by the right-hand post and allowed Famokun to roll the ball into the opposite corner, remarkably refusing to contest the spot kick.

The referee blew the final whistle immediately after the ball hit the back of the net, prompting tensions to boil over.

Bolivia's players sarcastically applauded the official as England's youngsters ran off celebrating.

Scenes soon turned ugly, with one Bolivian substitute sent off for attempting to attack the referee after a coach had angrily confronted the official.

England's players rushed in to protect the referee before several altercations broke out between the two sets of players.

FIFA officials were then forced to intervene, while England's youngsters further angered their opponents by celebrating in their faces. FIFA and the FA have been contacted for comment.

England's Under-15s walked off midway through their World Cup clash with Ireland

Similar scenes unfolded in the Africa Cup of Nations final earlier this year.

Morocco were awarded a controversial late penalty against Senegal, sparking a 15-minute protest as Senegalese players marched down the tunnel and refused to play on.

The game eventually resumed, Morocco's penalty was saved and Senegal went on to win in extra time.

However, the African federation subsequently stripped them of the title. That decision remains in dispute, though, with Senegal challenging the ruling at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Meanwhile, this was not the first England match disrupted at the tournament. On Tuesday, their tie against Ireland was rocked by a racism storm.

Young Lions boss Matt Thorpe withdrew his players in the 40th minute after one of them claimed an opponent had called him a 'monkey' moments after the England youngster pushed his opponent in the back.

A member of the Irish backroom staff shouted 'no, he didn't' while the English player remonstrated, sparking a shouting match between the two benches.

The England player approached his bench and waited on the touchline as Thorpe spoke to the fourth official. And just before play could resume, the England coach ordered his team off the pitch.

#2001. Raphinha at the double as Barcelona too strong for Aston Villa

Barcelona ensured Unai Emery had another Nou Camp nightmare as they beat his Aston Villa side 3-0 in the Champions League.

Lamine Yamal’s early opener and a second-half double for Europe’s most prolific scorer Raphinha, who has bagged 19 in 13 games this season, gave Emery a 55th birthday to forget.

The Spaniard will not be keen to return to this city any time soon as he has now lost 15 out of 16 matches at Barca, including the famous ‘Remontada’ nine years ago, when his PSG side lost a last-16 tie 6-1 to squander a 4-0 first-leg lead.

This was supposed to be a Red Letter Day for the club and was watched by super fan Prince William – a reward for their excellent progress in the four years of Emery’s reign.

It might have been more memorable had Villa taken a number of first-half chances to draw level, but defeat ends their 100 per cent start to the league phase.

Frank McAvennie apologises after criticising Celtic star's grief absence £750,000 padel club with four covered courts to open at Ayr United’s stadium

But with some winnable games still to come, they are still a good bet to finish in the top eight.

Barcelona have not found goals hard to come by this season, so the last thing Villa needed to do was hand out a freebie.

But they laid Barca’s opener on a plate in the seventh minute as playing out from a goal-kick went horribly wrong when Joao Gomes blindly passed straight to Yamal, who whipped a finish into the corner from 12 yards.

It was a nightmare start, but they could have been level within minutes as they caused chaos from two corners.

First, Matty Cash arrived late at the far post and his drilled effort was deflected wide and then the second delivery found its way through to Gomes, who thought he was about to make amends until Joao Cancelo produced a fine block.

Villa found their feet and began to expose Barca’s high line. It should have brought an equaliser in the 19th minute as Nicolas Jackson raced clear down the right and teed up Johan Manzambi, who dragged his shot wide.

Then Jackson was sent clear again and it looked like he would beat Joan Garcia to the ball, but the on-rushing Barca goalkeeper got a foot to it and made a vital tackle.

They did suffer another nervy moment when Zion Suzuki put his side in danger again when playing out from the back, but he made up for it by saving Anthony Gordon’s effort.

Villa again threatened as Manzambi surged into the box, but Garcia was equal to it.

Those missed chances proved important as Barca doubled their lead in the 52nd minute. Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha on the edge of the box and his effort deflected off Pau Torres’ heel and into the corner.

The third came 12 minutes later and it was a lovely goal as Cancelo skipped clear of John McGinn and picked out Raphinha, who made no mistake from six yards.

Leon Goretzka sent a glancing header against a post as Villa tried to get on the scoresheet, but the size of the defeat could have got out of hand.

Another poor Suzuki pass played Boubacar Kamara into trouble, with the Japan international denying Fermin from the resulting shot. Yamal, who became the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history, then whipped two efforts just wide.

#2000. Jack Grealish has let his team-mates down: This self-inflicted episode shows he lacks the hard graft and humility so desired by David Moyes - and the team were better off without him, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 17:58 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 09:36 EDT, 30 October 2026

Hard graft, humility and fighting for team-mates: three qualities not shown by a certain Jack Grealish this week.

They are also a trio of traits demanded by the Premier League's most experienced boss, David Moyes, who banished the once £100million man Grealish to the naughty step for missing training without permission.

News of his latest act of ill-discipline dominated every conversation on the Merseyside waterfront before this full-blooded contest with Newcastle but Grealish was not missed a jot as his youthful and energetic replacements put on a show.

Goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry were enough to send Moyes and Co to the Carabao Cup quarter-final and within sight of their first trophy since 1995, something the 63-year-old boss and these loyal fans crave above anything.

Moyes made the decision to drop and fine Grealish alongside chief executive Angus Kinnear. It is unknown if he will return for Monday's league game, also against Newcastle. The boss would not comment on the situation but said he supported the club decision to drop him.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it,' he said. 'All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch.

Jack Grealish let his Everton team-mates down, with the star suffering another setback

'From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job. It's a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them. There's humility about us tonight.'

Giant-slayers Fleetwood Town are up next. Given the way they toppled champions Arsenal on Tuesday, that will be no easy feat, but a trip to Highbury is all that stands between the Toffees and a first domestic cup semi-final since 2015-16.

Newcastle, meanwhile, look a pale imitation of the great team that beat Liverpool to win this competition in 2025 and the jury remains out on Matthias Jaissle. He lambasted his side's lack of maturity and said: 'It is shocking and it is frustrating as well.

'You need to be more mature and more clinical in these situations. Just clear it. It is a learning process but we don't have the time, we need to learn fast, especially with these young lads which is not an excuse any more.'

Fans around the country have tended to see the Carabao Cup as a chance to save some money in recent years and Everton supporters have grumbled at Moyes and former boss Sean Dyche for having a similar attitude with line-ups.

But a full house of 51,894 here – including 8,000 of the travelling Toon army – indicated that both teams were taking this seriously. Both mid-table with inconsistent form, this was a real chance for success.

Even the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, knew that and was in attendance alongside his wife Marie-France. There was an obvious joke to be made around this week's budget, which has given a helping hand to those in need this winter.

Given the Grealish-shaped hole in Moyes's team and the obvious lack of numbers in multiple positions, the Everton top brass might have fancied getting in Burnham's ear to get the chancellor's phone number and ask for a leg-up too.

Hackney volleyed in his first goal for the club following his summer move from Middlesbrough

Thierno Barry added Everton's third in the second half to set-up a tie against Fleetwood Town

Matthias Jaissle's side will seek revenge when the sides meet again in the league on Monday

Prime Minister Andy Burnham was among those celebrating as Everton bid to end their trophy drought

Moyes has had to muddle through the season with a dearth of outfielders following a botched transfer window, but he has made the best of a tricky situation – one that was not helped by Grealish's actions.

Any frustration at those off-the-field issues was parked on the night, though, as Everton found themselves two ahead at half-time. It was a scoreline to leave Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle cursing after a string of missed chances.

EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Pickford 7; Rohl 6, Tarkowski 7, O'Brien 7, Mykolenko 7 (Maitland-Niles 86); Hackney 8, Garner 7; Dibling 7 (Johnson 77), Dewsbury-Hall 8 (Norgaard 86), George 8 (Alcaraz 77); Barry 7.

Subs not used: Travers, King, Keane, Armstrong, Graham.

Scorers: Garner 34, Hackney 45, Barry 69.

Booked: Hackney, Dewsbury-Hall, Mykolenko, Pickford, Tarkowski.

NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5, Schar 5, Burn 6, Hall 6; Gonzalez 5 (Steur 81), Ramsey 5 (Joelinton 46); Murphy 5 (Toure 67, 6), Willock 5, Barnes 7 (Elanga 46, 6); Osula 5 (Wissa 46, 6).

Subs not used: Pope, Botman, Bamba, Thiaw.

As it was, Everton weathered the storm thanks to Jordan Pickford and several last-ditch blocks.

Despite Newcastle's territorial advantages, the Toffees settled and were first to strike on 34 minutes. It came through Grealish's direct replacement for a starting berth, Tyrique George, winning possession and, via Hackney, feeding Garner to pass into the far corner.

Hackney soon turned from provider to goal-scorer, although referee Farai Hallam might claim an assist. Good officiating saw him play an advantage when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was hauled down when charging goalwards.

Barry picked up a loose ball and fed Hackney who volleyed home, making it look easy when he could have easily fired over the bar. Seconds earlier, Harvey Barnes had been denied by Pickford but Newcastle were undone by a motoring counter-attack.

Moyes would be delighted with the two goals but arguably more buoyed by the defensive rearguard that followed. Jaissle responded by throwing on three half-time changes in Yoane Wissa, Joelinton and Anthony Elanga.

None of them worked as Everton played with their hearts on their sleeves in a warrior-like defensive display that had this new stadium rocking like rarely before. James Tarkowski put his body on the line and Sunderland lad Pickford made several inspired stops.

Barry put the icing on the cake on 69 minutes when Garner robbed Amar Dedic of possession and Dewsbury-Hall teed up the No9 to finish with composure and help his team one giant step closer to ending that trophy drought.

No Grealish? No problem. The Manchester City loanee, who showed his admirable side earlier in the day when he gave £10,000 to help an ill fan, has let his team-mates down with this latest episode.

But with a collection of young talents thriving, mixed with some soldier-like experienced heads and a boss with an appetite for silverware, Everton do not need Grealish right now.

This night was one to forget for him and Jaissle's work-in-progress Newcastle, who are a shadow of the halcyon days of Eddie Howe's cup-winning side, despite pulling one back late on through captain Dan Burn's header.

Everton fans including Mr Burnham, meanwhile, will have March 21 and a potential final at Wembley circled in their diaries.

#1999. Preston North End v Sheffield United: How Liam Kitching has helped defensive improvement

The Blades conceded almost twice as many goals last season as the campaign before, from 36 to 66. So far this term they have shipped 15 in 13 Championship games, and only second-placed Swansea City have kept more clean sheets.

One important factor has been the loan signing of Liam Kitching from Coventry City, but the Harrogate-born centre-back will be suspended at Deepdale after his fifth yellow card of the season.

Wilder has been delighted with the improvement, but insists it has not come at the price of positivity.

"It was something that we reviewed after last season – how many points we dropped from winning positions, what we needed to do, what we needed to lift," he revealed.

"The key is that you give yourself an opportunity to win games of football.

"We're a front-footed team. We don't go into games sitting off teams and playing on the counter-attack. It's not my way.

"But you have to make sure that individually you defend well, you don't make any mistakes.

"If there's one mistake, then somebody clears that out.

"Too many times last season one mistake went to two, three and four.

"So, having defenders that want to defend, having a team that wants to defend is really important."

Kitching played an important part as Coventry won last season's Championship, and has fitted in well at Bramall Lane.

"Every football club in the country has certain characteristics, doesn't it?" commented Wilder. "What makes a Sheffield United player? Liam pretty much seems to fit that bill, doesn't he?

"He's competitive going forward, personality, positive, trains well.

"I've known Liam a long time. Not personally, but through performances, playing locally, starting his career at Leeds United through to Harrogate and then to Forest Green and Barnsley. He played against us a few times for Coventry and won promotion.

"I look at that as well – players that have had success and know what it's like to win games.

"I think Liam's made a great difference to us. He's one that we're going to miss on Tuesday night.

"It's looked as if we're a little bit of a settled back four at the moment.

"There's nothing really tactical we've changed, it's just about dealing with when you're in possession and you're in control of the game."

The Blades have doubts over the former Leeds United trio of Kalvin Phillips, Patrick Bamford and Joe Rothwell after ankle, shoulder and groin injuries respectively.

"He's a tough boy and we've got to have tough boys mentally and physically," said Wilder after Phillips played through his problem against Wrexham.

"There's a bit of swelling, (but) that's calmed down. Fingers crossed he'll be available.

"Pat has a little bit of an issue with his shoulder. He's been working outside the last couple of days so a late decision will be made on him.”

Rothwell was due to be on the bench on Friday, but pulled out with a groin strain in the warm-up.

#1998. Matheus Cunha scores twice as Manchester United hit Roma with late fightback

Matheus Cunha’s late brace secured Manchester United a jaw-dropping 3-2 comeback win against Roma to breathe new life into their season and ease some of the pressure on Michael Carrick.

A nine-match winless run had left the Red Devils head coach’s job hanging by a thread and Tuesday’s wretched start in the Champions League only pushed him closer to the Old Trafford exit.

United were facing a fourth straight loss after Matias Soule’s avoidable opener was followed up by a Donyell Malen penalty in a first half that ended with boos.

Green and gold balloons had cascaded down the Stretford End as fans protested against the Glazers before the match, with the second half offering a reminder of the special spirit that underpins their club.

Raphinha at the double as Barcelona too strong for Aston Villa Scotland Women learn Nations League draw after promotion back to League A

Bruno Fernandes pulled one back from a retaken, and softly awarded, second-half spot-kick as United played with the kind of purpose and skill lacking this term.

That approach forced a late error that Cunha capitalised on, before the Brazil forward slammed in off the inside of the near post for the winner.

His celebration earned him the first of two quick bookings but the relief was as palpable as the delight as United held on for just their third win of the campaign.

"Joe Taylor said it after the game – Saturday doesn't count for much if we don't follow it up on Tuesday."

Luton were in the Premier League in 2024 but after showing patience with coach Jack Wilshere, Drury feels they are getting to grips with the transition to League One.

"When you've had success as a club and you've been in the Premier League, when you find yourself in League One you can have that entitlement or victim mentality," he said.

"You have to accept where you are and find a way to get success again.

"If you look at what Jack's done, their performance levels and the way that they look now to 12 months ago, they're so much better and I’m guessing that's because he's just made things better over time.

"Things take time and he's got good coaching staff around him with a good group of players.

"I'm pleased that he was given time because he was doing some really good things last season and this season they look even better.

"I'm under no illusions in terms of the challenge but our players feel confident and they almost take a step forward the greater the challenge, or they have done so far."

#1996. Huddersfield Town v Luton Town: Radinio Balker on 2026-27 Terriers spirit

Saturday's 3-0 win at Bradford City was one of the rare occasions this season coach Martin Drury has left a fit player out of a winning team, but Dutch centre-back Balker justified his return, and will be hoping to hold onto his place at home to Luton Town on Tuesday.

If he does not, there will be no hard flings.

"If you're a team, you also need to cheer when someone else in your position is doing well," says Balker. "I tried to do that last season when I wasn't playing.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"We have 46 games plus cup games, so altogether probably 58 to 60. I won't be able to play 60 games, unfortunately.

"But if we have capable players in the same area at the same kind of level, then it's always good for the team because everybody profits from a team-mate being good and also going up in leagues.

An adductor injury to Balker opened the door to Joe Low to make his first League One start of the season at Plymouth Argyle and he did so well defensively that Balker returned alongside rather than instead of him. But on top of that, Low scored a spectacular overhead kick at Valley Parade on Saturday.

"I'm just really happy for him because it hasn't been the easiest for him the first few months," grins Balker. "Last season he was starting most of the games and then this season not starting from the beginning is quite difficult.

"I always said to him to keep working hard. I was in a similar situation last season where I wasn't playing in the beginning but I kept working hard. I told him to do the same.

"If you look at what he's done the last four games, it's been amazing. And then to score a goal like that, that's amazing."

To see the smile on the 28-year-old's face makes you believe it is more than just a professional footballer trotting out the lines he thinks he ought to.

It is a selflessness Drury made his top priority in his first summer as coach, when Balker received a one-year contract extension – "a show of faith," he says – despite being unable to consistently show his best form over two injury-hit seasons.

"It was top of the list," says Drury when asked how important that mindset was in assembling this season's squad.

"If you want to build a culture, it's not about the footballer, it's about the man. It's about the human being.

"Alongside that is being available to play. They're the first two, and then we'll look at things after that in terms of their qualities and what they can bring to us as footballers."

Being a good team-mate is something Balker is conscious of.

"It's very easy if everything is going well," he admits.

"When you're injured or when you come from a different team and you're not starting, it's very easy to forget about those players, but they are just as important.

"I've been there myself so that's why I try to help where I can.

"I wouldn't say last season or the season before was bad, necessarily, but this season there's a different camaraderie, I would say.

"Maybe the wins help, I don't know, but definitely at the moment, I think it feels like everybody wants to fight for each other.

"People are allowed to show that they're not happy as long as it's not affecting the thing they have to do on the ball."

With four wins out of four – the same as Huddersfield - Luton will test the table-toppers' Terrier spirit on Tuesday – and in a very different way to how Bradford tried to.

"They've been in a good form, just like us," says Balker. "Even last season, even though they weren't at their best they played really good football, difficult to play against.

"It's going to be a good game. We have to win because we're at home and we're confident we can do that.

"We all know that there are different styles of football (between Bradford and Luton).

"I think this season the big difference is that we're not really changing a lot in the sense of how we approach a game. We don't have to change formation or we don't have to change how we press.

"We have certain ways that we have to press that you don't have to think about. That really helps for us to be okay with changing from a bit more direct to a bit more football."

Whatever Huddersfield face on Tuesday, they will face it together.

"You need a new group of men that are humble, that are selfless, that are willing to work," says Drury. "I think the (coaching) staff sense right now that all the players are quite enjoying spending time together, both on and off the pitch.

"But look, it's really early days. Let's see if they enjoy each other's company in a couple of months' time, when we're in the midst of December and January."

At times in a tough few years for Town, that spirit has buckled. It will not if everyone thinks like Balker.

#1995. Dave Challinor spoilt for choice as he looks for Sheffield Wednesday's golden blend

The principles Challinor, pictured, wants to see in blue-and-white stripes will have been hammered home on day one, putting into action the promises he will have made in a job interview which, given why Henrik Pedersen was sacked, will almost certainly have centred around front-footed, attacking football.

But when it comes to the formation, he almost has too much to choose from.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Luckily for him, his first two matches are in cup football and his third is likely to be postponed due to international call-ups. Not until the November 20 derby at Barnsley will he have to show his hand.

Of course his decision could be to not have a fixed formation at all. Some teams benefit from having a set shape, particularly those nearer the top of the table who aspire to dictate terms. But Challinor's Stockport County flitted between three and four at the back last season.

The task is always getting as many of your best players on the field in a way that makes the most of as many of them as possible.

Although it did not garner the win Challinor would have wanted as he watched from the Hillsborough stands, Matt Hamshaw's final – at least for now – match as caretaker manager showcased the team in a back three and a four, albeit a 4-4-1, after Sil Swinkels was sent off in the first half.

But the starting 3-4-2-1 will have given food for thought, with Callum Slattery, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Mason Burstow linking well with Jamal Lowe banned, Louie Barry injured, and Harry Gray, Keiran Morrison and Jordi Liongola benched.

“I was looking to see how I could get two up front and work backwards from there,” said Hamshaw. “It's just about finding a way to win.”

Despite Lowe's productive start to the campaign, centre-forward does not look the strong point of this squad. Keillor-Dunn can play as one but he too is a free spirit, better in the hole or at last as one of a pair. Slattery and Gray are best not tied to the wings.

The Owls also have plenty of solid centre-halves. Even with Liam Cooper and Di'Shon Bernard injured, they were still able to field Swinkels, Liam Palmer and Ernie Weaver, and have Gabriel Otegbayo on the bench.

Three at the back also makes it easy to get Max Lowe and Reece James – when fit again in four to six weeks' time – in the same side.

Giving Yan Valery freedom as a wing-back should get the best out of him too.

But by the same token, a fit Barry and Liverpool loanee Morrison are two of the better players, and most effective wide. Morrison is young and still erratic but a proper winger; the absence of wide attacker Barry seems to have hit the squad harder than it ought to have.

So perhaps a 4-2-3-1 or a 4-4-2 is in order.

Ultimately what did for Pedersen was the sense that he was not getting the best out of some talented ingredients. Finding the right mix is Challinor's challenge.

#1994. Pocognoli reveals plan to get best from returning McTominay, and from Scotland

As Scott McTominay returns to the Scotland squad, a nation expects. The current Tartan Army talisman was back among the list of names selected by Sebastien Pocognoli yesterday after recovering from a heart issue, and then immediately recovering his goalscoring touch with Napoli.

A disappointing World Cup in the summer, both collectively for Scotland and on a personal level for McTominay, is largely being put down in hindsight to the mild benign arrhythmia that left the midfielder struggling in the sweltering summer heat in the States.

“It was much harder,” McTominay explained after the tournament.

“Two days before the first match I felt unwell and didn’t know whether I’d play or not.

“It was tough to prepare myself mentally. Then, the high temperatures made the situation even more difficult. Looking back, it’s a huge regret of my career.”

Pocognoli, interestingly, has another theory about why McTominay never shone in the way that Scotland had hoped in the World Cup, citing a lack of structure in the team. Regardless, with a corrective ablation procedure safely behind him, McTominay is now back and raring to go, having bagged four goals in seven matches since his return to club football.

But his new manager is hoping that his masterplan can eventually lead to Scotland being a team that consistently carries a threat, rather than one that constantly looks to individuals like McTominay to produce moments of magic.

“It was a big reflection for me over the last weeks, to try and reduce the expectation here on two or three players,” Pocognoli said.

“The first thing is, why? When you have players who have made the difference in most of the games through individual actions or a situation from nowhere, it’s normal that people then expect them to do it in every game.

“But for me, I have to find a way of playing to give Robbo [Andy Robertson] an opportunity to score two or three goals like he nearly did in the last camp. Or to give John McGinn an opportunity to score. The strikers, Billy Gilmour - it’s about giving everyone the chance to shine as a collective.

“That will maybe decrease the expectation of one or two players. That’s something I’d like to try to do.

“It’s normal that people expect Scott to always be the best, if that’s what he’s had to deal with in the past. In the World Cup, it was less because the structure around him was less. But expectation was still big on him, it didn’t matter.

“It’s up to me to have a good structure around him so he can shine, but not only him - all of the players.”

All that being said, Pocognoli is as excited as any member of the Tartan Army to see McTominay back in the dark blue, and to see how he will fit into the system that he has implemented since taking the reins.

“I just want to know him a little bit more, from the personal aspect,” he said.

“We all know his quality. I think he can fit into the way we want to play. So, I’m just excited to see him on the pitch, to see if he can bring something extra in the way we want to play.

“Also, to see how he fits into the group with my own eyes. I want to make a real contact with him because before it has only been on the phone or by video call. I’m looking forward to meeting him.

“He’s a big player. He’s a very complete player on the pitch. Scott is good on the ball, he can infiltrate without the ball. He can press high on the pitch or he can be box-to-box.

“It’s a massive boost for us. My job is to combine his quality with other players around him and I think we will.

“I’ve watched most of his games. His first game back was difficult in the last 20 or 30 minutes which was normal. After that, he started to find his way again. He’s now ready. He’s scored goals playing in a similar shape as us at Scotland.

“It was good to see him higher and lower in that shape on the pitch. Is he hungry? Yeah. He was really disappointed to miss the first camp and was already talking about the next camp.

“At that point we weren’t sure because we had to see his rehabilitation. But he was excited to try his best to reach the November camp and he’s still excited now, which is good.

“He will bring experience, quality, an expectation of goals, a presence in the box - and he’ll bring leadership as part of the captain’s group.

“He has a strong voice. He’s a different character to the others but it’s up to me to produce the game plan for him and the players that allows him to shine, and not him to make the team shine, if you know what I mean? That’s the challenge.”
